stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis. Its velocity at time t seconds is \( v(t) = - t^{3} - 3 t^{2} + t + 2 \) meters per second, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the speed of the particle at time t = 1, and determine whether the speed is increasing or decreasing at that time. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The speed is 1 meters per second, and it is increasing at that time, because \( v(1) = -1 \) and \( a(1) = -8 \) have the same sign.

worked_solution.text: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, \( a(t) = - 3 t^{2} - 6 t + 1 \), so \( a(1) = -8 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: acceleration is the derivative of velocity

worked_solution.text: The speed is \( \left|v(1)\right| = 1 \) meters per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed is the absolute value of velocity

worked_solution.text: Because \( v(1) = -1 \) and \( a(1) = -8 \) have the same sign, the speed of the particle is increasing at t = 1.
worked_solution.rule_named: speed increases when velocity and acceleration share a sign

options.label: The speed is 1 meters per second, and it is decreasing at that time, because \( a(1) = -8 \) is negative, so the particle is slowing down.
options.derivation: the change in speed decided from the sign of the acceleration alone, without the sign of the velocity
